added_lines: How do we build trust in AI-native

In Episode 17 of The Path to 6G, Ross Cassan joins MJ Viscomi and Stephen Douglas to explore how AI traffic is shifting network assurance from packet performance to token performance. They discuss how digital twins and runtime guardrails help validate
decisions and enable safe rollback, while AI-powered assurance can detect problems earlier and accelerate root cause analysis.
Tune in for a conversation on AI trust and the future of autonomous networks:

Korea is helping shape the next generation of technology, with its leadership in semiconductors, memory, and communications playing an increasingly important role as AI transforms our industry. It was a pleasure to spend time with customers, partners, and the engineering community in Seoul at Keysight World Tech Day, where I shared my perspective on the accelerating pace of innovation and what it means for the future of AI infrastructure, 6G, and other emerging technologies.
As systems become more complex and interconnected, collaboration and the ability to validate new technologies earlier in development will be essential to moving innovation forward.
I also had the pleasure of meeting

, Professor at Seoul National University, whose pioneering invention of bulk FinFET technology has helped shape modern semiconductor design. It was fascinating to hear his perspective on the future of AI semiconductors, from low-power computing and memory innovation to emerging applications in robotics, space, and defense.

I left the event encouraged by the expertise and energy in the room, and grateful to everyone who joined us. Thank you to the Keysight Korea team for making the event possible. I look forward to building on this momentum together.
